summary: Holden Furber was a historian and Indologist who studied at Oxford and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1929). He taught at Harvard (~1930–1936), the University of Texas at Austin (1940, 1945–1948), and the University of Pennsylvania (1948–1973).

Linguist and Indologist Holger Pedersen studied at Copenhagen (Ph.D. ~1897), Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald under scholars including Verner, Thomsen, and Brugmann. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen, becoming professor in 1903 and succeeding Thomsen in 1912.

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

Holmes Welch worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his B.A. and M.A. at Harvard University (~1940–1957) and later served as a lecturer at Harvard (~1964–1976) and Yale University.

Hong Luo specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, earning a PhD from Peking University (2007). He worked at the China Tibetology Research Center (2007–2017), became professor at Sichuan University (2018), and was research fellow at Hamburg (attested 2026).
Hongyue Guo is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under Stephen R. Bokenkamp, also studying under Xubang Qi.

Honoré-Joseph Chavée was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Félix Nève at KU Leuven and Eugène Burnouf. He taught at the Royal Military Academy, Collège Stanislas, Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa (1862–1867), and École Supérieure de Guerre (1871–1873).

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996), and director at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University by 2004, studying under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.
Horace Arthur Rose worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Emmanuel College (~1886–1889) and served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1888 to 1917.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at Queens' College and SOAS (Ph.D. under Charles Otto Blagden), he served as Field Director for the Greater India Society (~1934–1941) and Vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1964–1968).

Indologist Horace Hayman Wilson studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital and Sanskrit under H. T. Colebrooke. He was Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860) and held posts at the East India Company, its Library, and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Indologist Horace Irvin Poleman earned his degrees at the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. 1933 under W. Norman Brown). He later served in the Library of Congress (1938–1949, 1955–1965) and as a U.S. Cultural Officer in New Delhi (1949–1952).

Horace L. Friess was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (~1915–1918) and Heidelberg, and taught at Columbia from 1919, serving as Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor of Human Relations from 1962 to 1966.

Horacio Francisco Arganis Juarez works in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the Autonomous University of Coahuila (attested 2001–2007), North Carolina State University (attested 2007), IEFAC (attested 2006), and the Instituto de Biología y Ciencias Humanas (attested 2006).
Horkhang Sonam Palbar was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Gendun Chophel (~1946–1951) and Tsadru Ngawang Losang.
Horst Brinkhaus is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Münster (~1978–1988) and Kiel University (~1988–2008).
Horst Fichtner, active in Indology and history/archaeology, earned a Dr. med. at the University of Leipzig by 1924 and taught social ethics at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1945.

Horst Lasic specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (1999), where he became a lecturer in 1999, and held a research post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1995.

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an epigraphist and scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India as Assistant Superintendent (~1904–1920) and as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).
